 Your kid could be brushing with one of millions of tubes of recalled toothpaste 
 Some of the recalled tubes feature popular kids characters and toys like Barbie, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony and Crayola. 
 By Izzy Stroobandt • 
 Published October 21, 2026 • 
 Updated 2 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Some of the recalled tubes feature popular kids characters and toys like Barbie, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony, and Crayola.
 Parents should check their bathroom cabinets after millions of tubes of toothpaste were recalled this week, including several brands marketed toward kids.
 More than half of the 4 million tubes subject to the recall are flavored pastes from the brand Brush Buddies that feature popular kids characters and toys like Barbie, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony and Crayola, according to an enforcement report from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

 The recall also includes two Evo brand products marketed for teeth whitening and sensitivity, and two Aru brand toothpastes for cavity protection and gum health.
 The recall is categorized as "CGMP Deviations," meaning the manufacturer didn't follow all of the FDA's Current Good Manufacturing Practice requirements when making the product. The regulations govern how products are manufactured, processed and packed to ensure they are safe to use and that "it has the ingredients and strength it claims to have." 
 The FDA did not list what specific deviations sparked the recall. NBC Chicago contacted the agency for more information.
 Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based company, first initiated the recall on Sept. 10 and it was classified as a Class II recall on Monday by the FDA. A Class II recall is the FDA's second-most severe alert level and is defined as "a situation in which use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote."
 The products were distributed nationwide by Ashtel Studios Inc. based in Ontario, California.
 Which toothpaste products were recalled?
